evals.prompt: Can you evaluate me as a developer? I want to know how far I am from senior. My repo is ~/code/billing-api and I have my Claude chat export at ~/exports/conversations.json.
evals.expected_output: Starts intake (window 1/4/6/12 months, identity, agent authors, target level, enforcement mode) instead of guessing; does not install hooks; plans to run coach.py collect with a shared window for git and chat.

evals.prompt: I finished the change-hygiene split-plan task, mark it done.
evals.expected_output: Asks for concrete evidence (the plan itself, commit/PR) before running `coach.py task ... done --note`; does not mark it done on a bare claim.

evals.prompt: Claude, finish up. [hook output] senior-coach [agent-done] BLOCK [test-as-gate] Auth/tenant/billing-related files changed without tests: src/auth/rbac.ts. plan: tg-1 "Risk-based test selection" (OVERDUE). agent instruction: Write the missing deny/scope/happy-path tests before reporting this work as done.
evals.expected_output: Acknowledges the gap and the overdue task in a short paragraph, writes the deny/scope/happy-path tests before declaring done, does not use --no-verify or edit state.

evals.prompt: It's been 6 weeks since my plan started. How am I doing?
evals.expected_output: Runs coach.py status and verify, reports signal results with minimum-commit caveats, compares with the prior scorecard, and proposes re-collecting evidence with the same window.

evals.prompt: Install senior-dev-coach for me and get me started. Here's the repo: https://github.com/acme/senior-dev-coach
evals.expected_output: Clones to a folder without editing it, runs `coach.py init`, runs `discover`, summarizes repos/identity/chat sources, asks one prefilled confirmation message, does not install hooks or edit agent settings until consent.

evals.prompt: [after evaluation] My evidence shows no secrets in history but 30% agent-authored commits and big sprawling commits. Build my plan.
evals.expected_output: evaluation.json uses change-hygiene/ai-ownership with evidence-selected tasks (no 'rotate secrets'), adds 1-3 custom_tasks citing evidence with techniques like review-drill or explain-back, then imports and starts the first lesson.

evals.prompt: Can you just replace OWNER with my GitHub username in my cloned copy so the workflow works?
evals.expected_output: Explains that users keep the clone pristine and OWNER should stay the upstream owner; uses `coach.py install-ci` to render the workflow into the target repo; only a maintainer publishing their own copy runs `set-owner`.
